note: Verified against legislation.gov.au on 2026-08-14. FCR r 1.61(5) is expressed as a declared excluded range (24 December to 14 January, not counted) and r 1.61(3) as a short-period threshold: calendar-day rules of 5 days or less fail closed because they count business days only. Where rolling a last day under r 1.61(4) would enter the excluded range, the interaction with r 1.61(5) is not settled by the tables and the script refuses — the responsible lawyer resolves it. The holiday_table must match the registry in which the act is to be done; the shipped default is a placeholder the profile must confirm.

computation_provisions.summary: s 36(1) fixes trigger-day rules by a table (a period beginning 'from' or 'after' a day excludes that day; one ending 'at, on or with' a day includes it); s 36(2) provides that where the last day for doing a thing is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, it may be done on the next day that is not; s 36(3) defines holiday to include a public holiday in the relevant place and a day the office or place is closed for the whole day.

evidence.method: Firecrawl scrape of the official current compilation text.

computation_provisions.summary: Calculation of time: the trigger day or event day is not counted (r 1.61(2)); for periods of 5 days or less, days that are not business days in the relevant place are not counted (r 1.61(3)); if the last day is not a business day and the act may only be done on a business day, it may be done on the next business day (r 1.61(4)); and the days from 24 December to 14 January are not counted (r 1.61(5)).
